findings.message:
does this always return an interrupt number? From the PCI docs on osdev wiki, i see this:
> For the x86 architecture, this register corresponds to the PIC IRQ numbers 0-15 (and not I/O APIC IRQ numbers). A value of 0xFF defines no connection.

So we'd want to possibly handle the 0xFF case specially, perhaps with an option.

Also, this doesn't include the interrupt pin info, which is probably a good thing to return along with the interrupt line. So this function could be something more like `pci_get_interrupt_info()` that returns an interrupt line and interrupt pin.

For more, see osdev wiki again:

> Specifies which interrupt pin the device uses. A value of 0x1 is INTA#, 0x2 is INTB#, 0x3 is INTC#, 0x4 is INTD#, and 0x0 means the device does not use an interrupt pin.

An enum for the interrupt pin would be the proper way to represent this.
findings.tp_fp_justification: 新增 pci_get_interrupt_line 把寄存器原始值当有效 InterruptNumber 返回，PCI 规范 0xFF 表示无中断连接，调用方会注册错误 IRQ。作者 'Sure, I'll change it' 并在 ed61b8703a 以 pci_get_interrupt_info 替换（0xFF→None）。
